html:
Jean-Bertrand Aristide is a former Catholic priest who in 1990 became the first freely elected president of Haiti. A preacher of liberation theology in the slums of Port-au-Prince, he won a landslide.

Seven months after taking office he was overthrown by the army in 1991. Thousands of his supporters were killed, and many Haitians fled by boat. In 1994 a US military intervention returned him to power to finish his term.

He was elected again in 2000, in a vote boycotted by the opposition. In 2004 an armed revolt and pressure from the United States and France forced him into exile in South Africa. He returned in 2011. His rise and falls followed the end of the Duvalier era and preceded the long crisis after the 2010 earthquake.
